 Police announced traffic arrangements from Nov. 14 to 15 to facilitate HZMB Half Marathon 2026
 Hong Kong 
 2026.11.13 20:00 
 Share to Wechat 
 Scan the QR code to share
 Police announced traffic arrangements from Nov. 14 to 15 to facilitate HZMB Half Marathon 2026. (File photo) 
 The Police announced today (Nov. 13) that special traffic arrangements will be implemented from Nov. 14 to 15 to facilitate the holding of Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge (HZMB) (Hong Kong Section) Half Marathon 2026. Members of the public are urged to plan their journeys in advance.
 The following temporary traffic arrangements will be implemented on the section of HZMB Hong Kong Link Road (HKLR) between the HZMB Hong Kong Port (HKP) and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Boundary, subject to the actual finishing time of the event and the reopening of the roads for vehicle use: Phase I (From 4 pm to about 11 pm on Nov. 14) 
 The left and middle lanes of the above section of HZMB HKLR (Hong Kong bound) will be closed, motorists heading for Hong Kong have to use the right lane of the above road section.
 Phase II (From about 11 pm on Nov. 14 to about 2 pm on Nov. 15) 
 All traffic lanes of the above section of HZMB HKLR (Zhuhai and Macao bound), the middle lane of the above section of HZMB HKLR (Hong Kong bound), and the slip roads leading to/from San Shek Wan Turnaround Facility will be closed.
 In connection with the road closures as mentioned above, the above section of HZMB HKLR (original Hong Kong bound) will be converted into two-way traffic, motorists heading for Zhuhai and Macao will be diverted to use the original Hong Kong bound road section.
 Phase III (From about 2 pm to about 4.30 pm on Nov. 15) 
 The left and middle lanes of the above section of HZMB HKLR (Hong Kong bound) will be closed, motorists heading for Hong Kong have to use the right lane of the above road section.
 A section of outbound goods vehicles (GV) lanes at the HZMB HKP after the GV Clearance Plaza will be temporarily closed from about 9 pm on Nov. 14 to about 3 pm on Nov. 15.
 Actual implementation of traffic arrangements will be made depending on traffic and crowd conditions in the areas. Members of the public are advised to exercise patience and tolerance and take heed of instructions from police officers on site.
 (Source: HK Police)
